why: A handle to a built-in nothing in the project could answer keeps no row (step 8, the built-in discard), and an Octave file answers no call (step 4; Octave is not read): once the empty script `lib/disp.m` (a script of nothing, step 11's ruling) turns to Octave, a file added later that takes `@disp` keeps no row, as a fresh index of the same files has it; the class's method `disp` is reached only through an object of the class (MATLAB doc 'Methods That Modify Default Behavior'). A sync in a long-lived process kept a failed row until step 13 (s402-c12, found by the step 11 fuzzer).
